title: Realizing Quantum Kernel Models at Scale with Matrix Product State Simulation
problem: Benchmarking quantum machine learning algorithms at practical scale has been limited by ineffective simulation methods. Existing quantum kernel implementations cannot handle realistic problem sizes with hundreds of features and thousands of training points.
motivation: Quantum state space offers an alternative function space for machine learning, but practical validation at scale remains absent from prior work.
method: The authors develop a quantum kernel framework using a Matrix Product State (MPS) simulator, which efficiently represents quantum states. They employ a circuit ansatz on a linear chain of qubits with systematically increasing interaction distances and evaluate performance on both CPU and GPU implementations to identify when GPU acceleration becomes advantageous.
key_novelty: First demonstration of quantum kernel models at practical scale (165 features, 6400 training points) using MPS simulation, significantly exceeding prior work capabilities.
contributions: Quantum kernel framework using Matrix Product State simulation
Scaling quantum classification to 165 features and 6400 training data points
CPU and GPU performance characterization with systematic interaction distance variation
Evidence that quantum model performance improves with feature dimension and training data

metrics.accuracy: Quantum model performance improves with feature dimension and training data scale

limitations: Limitations not discussed in provided abstract
primary_theme: Quantum kernel ML at scale via MPS simulation
